dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a set E, this is the finite sum over all omega of P.prob(omega) when omega belongs to E and 0 otherwise.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It computes the P-probability of the event appearing in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a function X from Omega to the reals, this is the weighted finite sum sum over omega of P.prob(omega) times X(omega).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to centered(omega)^2, it gives the second raw moment bounded by varianceBudget.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004

binders: An arbitrary type Omega equipped with a Fintype instance, hence a finite sample space.
A finite probability distribution P on Omega, with mass function p(omega) = P.prob(omega).
An arbitrary real-valued function centered : Omega -> Real.
Five real scalars bias, varianceBudget, biasRadius, kappa, and lambda.
hypotheses: The weighted second raw moment satisfies sum over omega in Omega of p(omega) * centered(omega)^2 <= varianceBudget.
The deterministic scalar bias satisfies |bias| <= biasRadius.
conclusions: Let A be the set of all omega in Omega such that |kappa * (centered(omega) + bias)| <= kappa * (sqrt(varianceBudget/lambda) + biasRadius). Then the probability of A satisfies P(A) >= 1 - lambda.
mathematical_definitions: The probability masses satisfy p(omega) >= 0 for every omega and sum over omega in Omega of p(omega) = 1.
For E contained in Omega, P(E) = sum over omega in Omega of p(omega) if omega is in E, and 0 otherwise; equivalently, P(E) = sum over omega in E of p(omega).
For X : Omega -> Real, the weighted expectation notation represented by LocalDef003 is sum over omega in Omega of p(omega) * X(omega).
The event in the conclusion is A = {omega : |kappa(centered(omega) + bias)| <= kappa(sqrt(varianceBudget/lambda) + biasRadius)}.
All magnitudes are ordinary scalar real absolute values, and sqrt(varianceBudget/lambda) is the nonnegative real square root.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite probability space, every real-valued function centered on it, and all real parameters bias, varianceBudget, biasRadius, kappa, and lambda, if varianceBudget and lambda are positive, kappa is nonnegative, the P-weighted second raw moment of centered is at most varianceBudget, and the absolute bias is at most biasRadius, then with P-probability at least 1 - lambda, the absolute value of kappa times centered plus bias is at most kappa times the sum of sqrt(varianceBudget/lambda) and biasRadius.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The sample space is restricted to a finite type and P is a discrete probability distribution.
Despite its name, centered is an arbitrary real-valued function. The proposition contains no assumption that its P-weighted mean is zero.
varianceBudget is only a positive upper bound on the second raw moment sum p(omega) * centered(omega)^2; it is not asserted to equal a variance.
There is no upper bound on lambda. When lambda >= 1, the lower bound 1 - lambda is nonpositive, so the conclusion follows trivially from nonnegativity of event probability.

kappa is allowed to be zero. In that case the event inequality is 0 <= 0 for every omega, so the event is all of Omega. For kappa > 0, the common factor kappa can be canceled from the event inequality.
No explicit nonnegativity assumption is placed on biasRadius, but |bias| <= biasRadius forces biasRadius >= 0 whenever the hypotheses are satisfiable.
If Omega is empty, no normalized P of the specified form can exist because its total mass would be 0 rather than 1; universal claims quantified over such a P are therefore vacuous on the empty type.
The proposition is entirely scalar: it contains no vector dimensions, vector norms, independence assumptions, or additional probabilistic structure.
bias is a fixed real scalar bounded in absolute value; it is not represented as a random variable or an expected value.
